transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Ever since my husband’s stroke, I just haven’t been handling everything the way I usually do, and I feel like I’m not coping with all these changes. It has just felt like too much lately.
Since your husband’s stroke, have you been feeling mostly overwhelmed and stressed about the situation, or have you also had persistent low mood or loss of interest in things most days?

I'm mostly just feeling overwhelmed, stressed, and constantly on edge rather than having a low mood. I backed out of my church activities and choir rehearsals not because I've lost interest, but because I am just worn thin trying to keep up with caregiving. I'm constantly struggling to stay on top of everything and worrying that I'm letting everyone down.
How long have you been feeling this overwhelmed and on edge—has it been more than 6 months, or did it start within a few months of your husband's stroke?

It hasn't been six months at all. These feelings started within a week or two of bringing my husband home from the hospital, which was about six weeks ago. So, I've really only been dealing with this for about a month now.
Have these stress and coping problems been causing major difficulties at work, home, or in your relationships, beyond what you would expect from the situation?

Yes, they've caused a lot of difficulties for me lately. I've had to back out of leading our church potluck and missed several choir rehearsals, and I've even missed paying a couple of bills on time. I've also found myself snapping at my friends from church because I'm just so on edge and worn thin, which isn't like me at all.
Have you been having any thoughts of harming yourself, or feeling so hopeless that you don't see a way to cope?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself at all. Even though I feel extremely overwhelmed, tired, and worried about managing everything, I've never thought about self-harm. I just want to find a better way to handle all these changes.
Since your husband's stroke, have you been having any nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling constantly on guard as if something bad is about to happen?

No, I haven't had any nightmares or flashbacks at all. While I do feel very on edge and tense, it's more from the daily stress of managing my husband's care rather than feeling like a specific bad event is about to happen.
Did these symptoms begin within 3 months of your husband’s stroke, and do they feel clearly tied to that stressor rather than happening out of the blue?

Yes, they absolutely did. I started feeling this way within a week or two of bringing my husband home from the hospital and taking on all these new caregiving duties. It is definitely tied to this sudden, overwhelming change in my life rather than happening out of the blue.
Have these symptoms gone away completely, or are they still continuing and causing problems in your daily life?

No, they haven't gone away and are still very much ongoing. For about a month now, ever since bringing my husband home, I've been struggling to keep up with my normal routine. I'm still falling behind on paying bills on time and haven't been able to go back to my church activities.
Have these stress-related symptoms continued for less than 6 months, or have they lasted longer than 6 months?

They have definitely lasted for less than six months, as it's only been about a month since I brought my husband home. I'm really hoping that once he becomes more independent and his care needs slow down, this rough patch will settle down within a few months.
Have you ever had a similar period of feeling overwhelmed or unable to cope after another stressful event in the past, or is this the first time this has happened?
No, I haven't really experienced anything like this before. I've usually been the one everyone else relies on, so feeling this way is completely new to me.
Just to confirm, did these feelings start within 3 months of your husband’s stroke and caregiving changes, and do they seem directly caused by that stress rather than by anything else?

Yes, they absolutely did. I started feeling this way within a week or two of bringing my husband home and taking on all his caregiving needs. It is definitely caused by the stress of managing his recovery and losing my usual routines, rather than anything else.
Did these symptoms begin within 3 months of your husband's stroke and the caregiving changes, and do they seem clearly tied to that stressor rather than happening for no clear reason?

Yes, they absolutely did. I started feeling this way within a week or two of bringing him home and taking on all those caregiving responsibilities. It is entirely due to this sudden, overwhelming change in our lives and not for any other reason.
Have these stress-related symptoms been improving as you adjust, or are they still getting worse or staying about the same?

They really haven't improved much and have been staying about the same, which still feels quite overwhelming. These struggles with feeling on edge and unable to keep up have been going on consistently for about a month now, which is why my daughter urged me to seek help.
Have your stress and coping symptoms started to improve at all as you’ve adjusted to your husband’s care, or are they still about the same and causing problems in your daily life?

No, they haven't improved and are still about the same. These struggles with feeling overwhelmed and unable to cope have been going on for about a month now, and they continue to cause problems like making me miss bill payments and pull back from my church activities.
Have these symptoms gone away now that the stressor is easing, or are they still continuing and causing problems in your daily life?

No, they are still very much ongoing since my husband is still recovering and I am managing his care every day. The social worker did reassure me that once he is more independent this rough patch should resolve within a few months, but right now I've been struggling like this for about a month and am still right in the middle of it.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed emotional and behavioral symptoms within 1-2 weeks of an identifiable psychosocial stressor (husband’s stroke and new caregiving demands), with prominent overwhelm, tension/on-edge feelings, worry, irritability, and reduced functioning. Symptoms began within 3 months of the stressor, have lasted about 1 month, and are causing clear impairment, with no evidence of major depressive episode, PTSD, or another primary disorder. This is most consistent with adjustment disorder.
